title: Error reduction for bounded-error log space
statement: Let $L$ be a language over the Boolean alphabet that belongs to bounded-error probabilistic logarithmic space, and let $d$ be a natural number. There exist a natural number $c$ and a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet such that, for every input $x$ and every sequence of nondeterministic choices, $M$ uses at most $c(\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+1)$ work-tape cells. Moreover, for every input $x$ there is a natural number $T$ such that every choice sequence of length $T$ makes $M$ halt on $x$, and the probability that its output is the membership bit of $x$ in $L$ is at least $1-(1/2)^{(|x|+1)^d}$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language over the Boolean alphabet and belongs to BPL
